p01: Lineage is comic cutout collage. Forage public-domain engravings (a rubber boot or wellington from a trade catalogue or encyclopaedia plate, a trout from a natural-history plate, river-bed stones) from Wikimedia Commons, cut them out, and assemble the giant boot on a table with visible scissors-cut edges and drop shadows, hinged at the ankle. The boot blocks an amber lamp beam.
p03: Lineage is a classroom chalkboard. Handmade: build a real slate board with wood frame and dusty surface, and letter HOOK MONSTER in chalk one stroke at a time with a chalk stick, then the chalk sketch of the monster beside it. The rule is a lipogram shown as washed chalk: part of the lettering is wiped by a wet cloth and the reading changes. Trout pupils are cut-paper pieces with satchels, not smiley faces.
p14: Lineage is atmospheric multiplane cutout animation. Handmade and/or foraged: one crimson maple leaf (a foraged public-domain photograph or herbarium scan of a real maple leaf, cut out, is ideal) sinking through several painted glass planes of murky river with real depth and parallax. Show the planes being stacked one by one before the leaf is laid in.
p35: Lineage is a 1940s documentary photograph archive. Forage public-domain FSA/OWI-era photographs from Wikimedia Commons (rural mailboxes, a canvas mail sack, a country post office; Library of Congress scans hosted on Commons are fine, the LOC site itself is unreachable). Make a document montage on a table: prints laid down, a paper mailbox numbered 44 cut and pinned, letters spilling as cut paper.
p44: Lineage is a spinning optical disc with words set in a spiral. Handmade: typeset your own original spiral sentence about the river (not any existing text) on a black and white disc, show the disc being inked ring by ring and the letters set one at a time, then spin it at speeds where the spiral seems to advance and recede. The rule is a spiral palindrome if you can manage one; say honestly in the note if it is only near.
